refines ACT-04 (The generated sendTask 'Place orders with several online stores' (X3) has no counterpart in the reference, where the same step is a userTask 'Place order' (M1). The description (S5) says the actor orders the materials from several online stores, which is work the actor performs and not a message exchange. The mistake is the choice of element type, not a missing element. The guideline is stated gen)

The records do not support a new guideline that the generated model should follow. Several reference elements have no basis in the description: the 'Get order' intermediate catch event (the description says only that the order is processed, with no wait for a result), the 'finished house' end event after 'Build tree house' (the description says only that invitations are sent after the house is built), and the manualTask choices 'Call friends' and 'Hire building company' (the description says messages are sent to friends). The reference therefore conflicts with the description on these points,

The label pairs (P2, P3, P5) show the generated labels follow the description's own wording ("create the list of needed materials", "build the tree house", "want to build a tree house"). The divergence comes from the reference labels, so the generator is not at fault and no label guideline is supported. M6 ("Hire building company") has no basis in the description, so the reference contradicts it there. The order-placement gap (M1) is already covered by the previous guideline, which the tools did not return, so I did not duplicate it. The remaining missing elements (M5, M13, M14) rest on wordin

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process asks outside helpers to carry out physical work, and the next step follows once that work is done, but the description names no message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for: Model the helpers' physical work as a manual task placed in the sequence before the next step that depends on it. Do not model the completion of that work as an intermediate catch event, and do not add a receive event for it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process asks outside helpers to carry out physical work, and the next step follows once that work is done, but the description names no message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process sends messages to outside people asking them to carry out work, and it names no reply, message or condition that the process waits for before continuing: Model the sending of the requests as one send task labeled with the sending action and its content as the description states them, placed where the description places the sending. Model the work those people carry out as a separate manual task placed after the send task, in the sequence where the description says that work is needed. Do not merge the sending and the work into one task, do not label the sending as a call or a generic step, and do not add an intermediate catch event for a reply the description does not state.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process sends messages to outside people asking them to carry out work, and it names no reply, message or condition that the process waits for before continuing

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process sends work, requirements, or items to an outside party, or receives items or results back from one, and at least one of these exchanges is named in the description: Model each such outside party as its own bpmn:participant pool, named with the role the description gives it. For every send step, add a message flow from that step to the party's pool. For every returned item or result the process waits for, add an intermediate catch event in the process pool with a message flow from the party's pool to that event. Before finishing, check that each outside-party pool has at least one message flow to and at least one from the process when the description names both directions, and that no pool is left with no message flows. Do not represent these exchanges with sequence flows across pools.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process sends work, requirements, or items to an outside party, or receives items or results back from one, and at least one of these exchanges is named in the description

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the actor sends messages to several other people so that they carry out work for the actor, and the description gives no message content, no reply, and no formal message exchange with a receiving party: Model the contacting as a bpmn:manualTask labeled with the contacting action as the description words it, placed where the description places it in the sequence. Do not model it as a bpmn:sendTask, because no message is exchanged with a process participant. Connect it with sequence flows to the surrounding steps, and model any later work the people perform as a separate task only when the description states it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the actor sends messages to several other people so that they carry out work for the actor, and the description gives no message content, no reply, and no formal message exchange with a receiving party

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the actor personally carries out an action toward several outside suppliers (for example, placing requests or orders with several external vendors) and does not describe a message exchange or a response as the unit of work: Model that action as a user task performed by the actor, placed where the description places it in the sequence. Do not model it as a send task, because the send task would represent a message rather than the actor's performed work. Use a send task only when sending a message is itself the described unit of work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the actor personally carries out an action toward several outside suppliers (for example, placing requests or orders with several external vendors) and does not describe a message exchange or a response as the unit of work
